label: Question 1
t: More time for Senate to act on judicial appointments
threshold: majority of votes on the question, equal to at least 50% of all ballots cast (blank votes count as no)
what: Gives the state Senate 60 days instead of 30 to consider and act on appointments of justices and judges made between April 1 and December 31, when the Senate is not in regular session or is about to adjourn. The 30-day window stays for other appointments.
y: The Senate gets 60 days to act on judicial appointments made April–December outside regular session.
n: The 30-day window stays year-round, often requiring special sessions.
fiscal: No official fiscal estimate. Sponsor Sen. Karl Rhoads cited about $5,000 per special session in neighbor-island senators' airfare and per diem that could be avoided.
con: Judiciary administrative director Rodney Maile raised concerns about longer vacancies (courts took no formal position)

label: Question 2
t: County RISE bonds for housing infrastructure
threshold: majority of votes on the question, equal to at least 50% of all ballots cast (blank votes count as no)
what: Directs the Legislature to let counties issue Resilient Infrastructure for Shelter and Equity (RISE) bonds, a form of tax-increment financing, for public improvements in designated districts. The bonds would be repaid only from future growth in property-tax revenue in those districts, not from higher tax rates, and would be excluded from county debt limits, subject to oversight rules set by law.
y: Counties could use RISE bonds to pay for infrastructure that supports housing, outside their debt limits.
n: RISE bonds stay unavailable; infrastructure continues to be funded by developers, regular county borrowing or general funds.
fiscal: No official fiscal estimate. Bonds are repaid solely from property-tax growth within designated districts and may not be repaid by raising property-tax rates.
pro: Hawai'i Association of Realtors, NAIOP Hawaii, Sen. Troy Hashimoto, Pacific Resource Partnership

reasons.housing: Gives counties a new way to finance roads, water and sewer lines needed for housing, especially near transit.
reasons.fiscal: New county bonds would sit outside county debt limits, with repayment tied to future property-tax growth in each district.
